page: Microsoft Azure D2lds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance features 2 vCPUs mapped from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, supported by 4.0 GB of system memory, which equates to a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD for storage and utilizes the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and int8 operations.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2108.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.39 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance is limited. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 1984.89 and Geekbench multi-core score of 2627.0 are relatively weak, reflecting the physical single-core hardware constraint. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached large-block read speeds at 21.01 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.28 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also fall into lower performance tiers, with Redis achieving 2.94 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring high clock-speed single-threaded execution without demanding large memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and the shared physical core architecture for the two virtual threads, which limits parallel processing efficiency. This server is appropriate for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, small-scale text processing, and low-intensity utility workloads that benefit from fast single-core CPU speeds and local NVMe storage but do not require substantial RAM or multi-threaded scaling.
